headline: Self-Direction reports persistent LoRA adapters that improve agent task recovery across benchmark suites
summary: The Self-Direction preprint describes a loop that converts a verified agent failure into procedural examples and a task-specific LoRA adapter, then routes and reuses that adapter on related tasks while keeping base weights fixed. The authors report accuracy rising from 38.8% to 55.8% on 165 GAIA tasks, from 64.4% to 73.3% mean across three runs on 161 Claw-Eval tasks, and from 51.7% to 65.5% mean across three runs on 89 Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks. These are paper-reported benchmark results; the method needs a verified failure signal and additional reflection/training resources, and the research desk has not reproduced them. The authors’ linked implementation page and the preprint differ on whether GAIA reflections received reference answers; the exact evaluated prompt inputs remain unresolved.
